analysis: What changed versus the 5:00 AM brief: futures barely moved in net terms but the S&P leg slipped (S&P futures -0.07% at 7:36 a.m. ET to -0.2% in IBD's later morning read; Dow steady near -0.7%, Nasdaq steady near +0.3%) — the same split tape into the open. Pfizer faded from +0.6% premarket at 5:00 AM to edging lower in IBD's later read, a reminder that this morning's beats are not holding gains. The chip bounce broadened (SOXX +2.70% after -3.79% Monday, with SanDisk, Micron, AMD and Intel all up) while software stayed sold (Salesforce, Datadog, Atlassian all down ~3%), so the bounce is narrow, not a broad risk-on turn. The Nasdaq-100 correction framing hardened: Monday's close put it more than 10% below its October 6 record, its third correction of 2026, with semis down ~12% in three sessions — that is the backdrop AMD reports into after the bell. Signal vs noise: AMD's print, the 10:00 a.m. ET JOLTS/factory-orders data, and the USAC call at 11:00 a.m. ET are today's real catalysts; Polymarket midterm odds (Democrats 78% Senate, 95% House per IBD) are positioning chatter until results land overnight; the Nasdaq 23/5 December launch note is structural context, not a price driver for today.
disclaimer: Not financial advice — for informational purposes only.

headlines.headline: Futures mixed into the open (IBD live coverage, later morning read): Dow futures -0.7% (down 300+ points), S&P 500 futures -0.2%, Nasdaq-100 futures +0.3%; SPY -0.2% and QQQ +0.3% premarket.
headlines.why_it_matters: S&P futures slipped from -0.07% at 7:36 a.m. ET to -0.2% while Dow/Nasdaq held — election-day caution in blue chips, tech stabilization holding for now.

headlines.headline: Apple still down ~4% premarket, set to open at its lowest since Sept. 10, even after beating fiscal Q4: EPS $2.10 vs $1.99 expected, sales $114.5B vs $113.4B expected — the holiday-quarter gross-margin guide of 45-46% (with rising memory costs) is doing the damage (IBD).
headlines.why_it_matters: A beat sold on margin guidance — the market is pricing memory-cost pressure into the December quarter, not the September beat.

headlines.headline: Chips bounced broadly: SOXX +2.70% after -3.79% Monday, with SanDisk +4.90%, Micron +3.56%, AMD +3.00% and Intel +2.85%; Nvidia +1.67% after four straight losses (Swingfolio/Reuters). AMD reports after the close; Wall Street expects EPS $1.95 on revenue $13.1B (IBD).
headlines.why_it_matters: The most beaten-down group is stabilizing into AMD's print — the bounce needs an earnings confirmation to become a reversal.

headlines.headline: Palantir tumbled 6%+ premarket after beating Q3 earnings and revenue targets, as new contract growth slowed; shares are on pace for a sixth straight losing session after breaking their 50-day line Monday (IBD).
headlines.why_it_matters: Another beat sold on a deceleration metric — valuation names are being charged for any slowing growth signal.

headlines.headline: Other earnings movers held the same pattern: Shopify still down ~16% premarket, Dynatrace plunged nearly 14%, Ferrari rose 2%+, Yum Brands jumped close to 4%, and Pfizer edged lower — fading from its +0.6% premarket gain at 5:00 AM (IBD).
headlines.why_it_matters: Beats are not holding gains this morning — breadth of the sell-the-beat pattern matters more than any single name.

headlines.headline: Megacaps split in late premarket (Finnhub, 8:56-8:58 a.m. ET): Amazon +1.12%, Tesla +0.84%, Meta +0.26%, Microsoft -0.31% versus Monday's close.
headlines.why_it_matters: No single megacap direction — Amazon/Tesla firmness offsets Microsoft softness, consistent with the mixed futures tape.

headlines.headline: Midterms today, macro at 10:00 a.m. ET: September JOLTS job openings (7.1M expected vs 7.09M prior) and factory orders (+1.1% expected vs +0.1% prior); polls favor Democrats retaking the House, Polymarket puts Democrats at 78% for the Senate and 95% for the House (IBD/Swingfolio).
headlines.why_it_matters: Results emerge overnight, so traders carry election risk with no scheduled announcement to trade against; strategists cited by IBD argue a blue wave would be bad news for AI stocks.

headlines.headline: Oil kept rebounding: WTI crude futures up to around $97.50 a barrel (IBD); Brent up ~1% to ~$105-106 after Monday's ~8% slide reversed on reports of the U.S. strike on Iran's Qeshm Island and an Iranian official saying a deal was far off.
headlines.why_it_matters: The prior session's biggest tailwind keeps reversing — higher crude re-tightens the inflation headwind into the open.

headlines.headline: Nasdaq-100 confirmed in correction: Monday's close was more than 10% below its October 6 record, its third correction of 2026, with the semiconductor benchmark down ~12% in three sessions and the index now below its 200-day EMA (XTB/Reuters).
headlines.why_it_matters: Correction status frames every tech bounce as guilty-until-proven-innocent — AMD after the bell is the next proof point.

headlines.headline: Nasdaq's 23/5 trading launch (Dec. 6) moved a step closer: NasdaqTrader notes the dedicated market-data products for the new 9:00 p.m.-4:00 a.m. ET session are now available for onboarding, with a one-hour 8:00-9:00 p.m. ET pause retained.
headlines.why_it_matters: Structural, not a today price driver — overnight sessions will eventually let earnings and macro news trade outside regular hours.

market_snapshot.breadth_notes: Prior regular session (Mon Nov 2): rotation, not broad selling — 8 of 11 sectors rose (consumer discretionary +2.39%, financials +1.82%, materials +1.74%) while tech fell 2.94% and energy 3.93%; equal-weight S&P 500 rose 0.76% while the cap-weighted index fell 0.51%. Nasdaq-100 closed more than 10% below its Oct 6 record (third correction of 2026). No S&P 500 advance/decline ratio or volume-vs-20-day-average figure shown in this morning's sourced pages.

usac.why_it_matters: No fresh USAC news since the 5:00 AM brief's Q3 print (revenue $357.2M vs ~$348.32M consensus, Adjusted EBITDA $197.3M, DCF coverage 1.67x, distribution held at $0.525).
